title: Turn it like Trimble: a year of precision on and off the pitch
summary: Watch the new Turn it like Trimble video, see a year of Trimble technology at work across Anfield and enter to win an LFC shirt signed by three players.
body_markdown:
Every matchday at Anfield depends on work most fans never see, from the structure of the stands to the hospitality spaces. That work depends on precision and technology, which makes Liverpool Football Club and Trimble a natural fit. In October 2025, the two organizations announced[a multi-year partnership](https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/trimble/article/trimble-liverpool-football-club-a-partnership-built-on-teamwork) built on a shared belief: teamwork drives success. In the year since, the partnership has come to life through a series of hands-on projects in the stadium and in the community.


At Anfield, Trimble[scanned the Kop](https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/trimble/article/mapping-passion-precision-anfield-stadium) with a Trimble X9 and a Trimble SX12, giving the club a living record of a stand that has seen extensive renovations over the decades. Trimble SketchUp also helped interior designer Jenny Denton deliver the new[Japan Airlines (JAL) Lounge at Anfield](https://www.trimble.com/en/blog/trimble/article/liverpool-fc-anfield-stadium-jal-lounge-sketchup-3d-design) . And in the community, the Trimble Foundation and LFC Foundation gave about 80 young people a first look at careers they might not otherwise have considered, with hands-on time at Anfield using Trimble SketchUp, Tekla Structures, Trimble SiteVision and a Trimble X9 scanner.


Now, three Liverpool FC players put that teamwork on screen in a new Turn it like Trimble trailer.


## A new way to Turn it like Trimble


The campaign features Dominik Szoboszlai, Ryan Gravenberch and Kostas Tsimikas. It shows how precision and connected data shape results on the pitch, in the office, on the job site and beyond.


In football, a turn is the moment a player receives the ball, reads the space and sends play in a new direction. Every turn depends on the pass that came before it and the teammate ready for what comes next. At LFC, action on the pitch is driven by a highly trained team of specialists working as a cohesive unit, using every bit of data and technology available to gain a competitive edge.


Trimble customers work the same way, connecting people, data and workflows across project lifecycles to deliver on time and on budget. Construction teams, surveyors and transportation crews pass information from the office to the field and back again. When those handoffs are precise, teams turn resources into results.


To celebrate the launch of our new Turn it Like Trimble campaign, Trimble and Liverpool FC are giving one fan an official club shirt signed by our featured players, Szoboszlai, Gravenberch and Tsimikas.


## What comes next


In its first year, the partnership has put Trimble technology to work in the stands, in the stadium's hospitality spaces and at a STEM camp for young people. As Anfield changes, its digital record will grow along with it, and there are more spaces to design and more measurements to make.


As Trimble CEO Rob Painter said when the partnership launched, "Our partnership with Liverpool FC is about how connecting people, data, and workflows creates a competitive edge, giving our customers the confidence to succeed every day."


Keep an eye out for the new ad during matches across the US and UK, or check out the full-length version on the[partnership page](https://trimble.com/en/learn/liverpoolfc-partnership) , where you can discover the many ways Trimble and LFC are taking teamwork to the next level. There’s more to come in 2027, so be sure to follow Trimble on[LinkedIn](http://linkedin.com/company/5160/) for the latest news and updates about the partnership and beyond.
